title: Stop showing raw e.toString() as the device-restore error message in RestoreStatus/DeviceRestoreService
rule: EH-5 / AX-2 (no pre-formatted human messages; ARB-only user text)
why: RestoreStatus.error(message: String) is a raw String, not a code/enum, and DeviceRestoreService feeds it e.toString() directly — a raw exception message (e.g. 'Exception: Data pull failed: [firebase_firestore/unavailable] ...'). device_restore_screen.dart renders this string verbatim next to a properly-localized l10n.deviceRestoreFailed headline (lines 214-222), so any restore failure — plausible on flaky mobile networks, which this cloud-restore flow specifically targets — shows raw, untranslated, technical English text to Hebrew-locale users today, live, with no masking guard. Separately, RestoreStatus.restoring's `phase` field is a hardcoded English sentence matched by string equality in _localizePhase(); the two files' string literals must stay in lockstep by convention only — if either drifts, the fallback silently renders the raw English phase instead of erroring.
recommendation: Replace RestoreStatus.error's free-text `message` with a stable error code/enum resolved via AppLocalizations in the screen (mirroring how `phase` already works, but with a sealed type instead of string matching so drift is a compile error).
acceptance_criteria: RestoreStatus.error carries a typed code (enum or sealed subtype), not a raw String built from e.toString().
A Locale('he') widget test pumps a forced restore failure and asserts the rendered error text is 100% ARB-sourced (no raw exception text).
phase and the error code share one sealed type/enum between DeviceRestoreService and the screen so an unmapped case fails to compile instead of silently falling back to English.
